title: Send It Pod
logline: Two climbing podcast hosts argue about the worst summit attempt of their lives (she fell asleep on the ridge, standing up). When she asks what's in his pack now, the answer on the desk is {{product.name}}, and it isn't for the mountain.

worn: glasses, headphones, hats, fleeces, watches and socks pulled from a stuff sack and put on at the desk; footwear is shown, not worn, on camera
handheld: bottles, headlamps, earbuds, chargers and tools set down by the mic

avoid: climbing safety equipment (ropes, harnesses, helmets): the punchline says it isn't for the mountain
anything unsafe to use while talking into a mic (sedatives)

lore: Send It Pod records every Tuesday night in Kofi's converted one-car garage in Boulder. Tonight is episode 148; his late dad's workbench is still under the shelves and the old oil stain is still under the rug.
Brynn and Kofi were rope partners for nine seasons before she went full-time as an alpine guide (about 60 days a year on the ice) and he started drawing trail maps for a living.

The story everyone asks for: Kessik Peak, 2016, 4:10am on the summit ridge, Brynn fell asleep standing up, clipped to an anchor, for eleven minutes. Kofi took a photo. It hangs in a thin brass frame on the back shelf.
The chunk of grey granite on the desk came off Kessik's summit block that morning. They use it as a paperweight for the listener questions.
Every rope on the shelf has a story and a strip of coloured tape on its end: orange for retired, green for still in service.

beats.summary: Cold open mid-story: Brynn confesses she fell asleep on a summit ridge, standing up.
Kofi was roped to her. She protests: hour fourteen! He reminds her what she packed instead. She fires back: so what's in your pack, genius?
Kofi produces the product at the desk, the product moment lands on the mic, and he names it with one benefit.
She assumes it's for climbing. It isn't: he needs it here, because she talks for three hours.
Brynn collapses laughing into her mic. That's fair.
Wide two-shot, the product between the mics; Brynn does a deadpan host-read of the tagline.
